why: Rule 1: the 5.2 cm proton stub falls monotonically 250k->50k toward 10005, so it starts there and Braggs at 10000, while the 82 cm muon leaves 10005 flat at MIP.
Rule 1 plus rule 2 on a lone contained 240 cm muon: MIP the whole way with a stopping spike only at 20000, so 20001 is the cool start end and it is the low-z one, with the track beam-forward.
Rule 1 at 20002: the 146 cm muon leaves MIP and Braggs at 20000 while the 40 cm proton chain 20006+20005 rises 80k->260k away from 20002, and 20002 is the lowest-z junction.
Rule 1 at the degree-3 hub 12004: the 10.5 cm proton rises 105k->215k away from it and both electron prongs also start there, and it is the lowest-z point of the cluster.
Rule 1 read on the p4 profiles: all three prongs (proton to 350k, pi+, muon) start at about 20k right at 22003 and get hotter away from it; the 155 cm muon just exits the x wall beyond 22002.

Rule 3 removes 13001, where the 246 cm track has a monotone Bragg rise to 150k with a blue 25-40k Michel on that same end, and rule 1 then leaves 13000 as the only cool end the track gets hotter away from; the tier is low because the track runs backward in z from 13000 and no prong corroborates it.

Kink at 14002 with a MIP muon on one side and an 8.7 cm prong sitting uniformly at 110-130k on the other; a 2.7x-MIP prong is a hadron and not a Michel, and the 200k on the muon's last two points is vertex-region overlap rather than a Bragg shape.

The two clusters are 12.8 cm apart, and the 26 cm proton's backward line of flight passes within 2.4 cm of the muon end 22001 while the muon's backward line misses the proton start by 16 cm, so the common origin is 22001 with the proton's first centimetres unreconstructed.

Rule 1 in its cleanest form: both prongs rise away from 15002, the 199 cm muon toward the x wall and the 83 cm proton rising 60k->140k to its Bragg at 15001, the prongs are 125 degrees apart so not the collinear trap, and 15002 is lowest in z.

Rule 1 at the degree-4 hub 24003: the 24.6 cm proton rises 25k->290k away from it and the 21 cm electron prong 10k->220k, and the whole EM/hadronic spray fans out from this point; only the 3.3 cm split from 24002 that carries the long muon keeps this off certain.

Rule 1 with all three prongs starting near 32k at 8008 and rising away, the 8008-8007-8004 chain being one continuously rising 24 cm proton, and the 183 cm muon's backward line from 4001 passing within 1.6 cm of 8008 across the 21.6 cm gap.

Rule 1 at the only real junction: the 42 cm track rises away from 2001 toward its hotter end at 2000 and a 3.1 cm 97k proton stub goes back the other way, and 2001 is the low-z junction of a small, otherwise featureless event.

The zoom shows a clean V at 16002 with a MIP muon arm running out to z=498 and a proton arm rising green to dark red into a Bragg at 16004, plus a short hot stub; nothing rises toward 16002, and the rival 16005 is a 158-degree collinear hot blob.
Rule 8 territory: a lone 138 cm MIP track at constant x with both ends interior, flat dQ/dx and no Bragg at either end, so there is no direction evidence at all and only rule 2 (lower z) picks 26001.

Rule 1 read on shape: the 11000 end has a broad 15 cm monotone rise to 170k (a real Bragg) while the 11001 end has only a single-point 245k spike plus several sub-cm blobs within a few cm, and the 275 cm muon runs strongly beam-forward from 11001.
